definitions.explanation: A tendency to suspect and distrust others' motives. Describes a deep-seated, often irrational mistrust.

examples.japanese: {猜疑心|さいぎしん}が{強|つよ}い{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: That person is very suspicious of others.

examples.japanese: {猜疑心|さいぎしん}から{誰|だれ}も{信|しん}じられなくなった。
examples.english: Because of suspiciousness, they couldn't trust anyone anymore.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{裏切|うらぎ}りが{彼|かれ}の{心|こころ}に{深|ふか}い{猜疑心|さいぎしん}を{植|う}え{付|つ}けた。
examples.english: Years of betrayal planted deep suspiciousness in his heart.

notes:
A literary word describing a deep, persistent tendency to distrust others. Composed of {猜疑|さいぎ} (suspicion, jealousy) + {心|しん} (heart, mind). The character {猜|さい} specifically implies jealous suspicion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猜疑心|さいぎしん}が{強|つよ}い: to be very suspicious
- {猜疑心|さいぎしん}を{抱|いだ}く: to harbor suspicion
- {猜疑心|さいぎしん}に{駆|か}られる: to be driven by suspicion
- {猜疑心|さいぎしん}の{塊|かたまり}: a bundle of suspicion (very distrustful person)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {疑|うたが}い: doubt, suspicion — everyday word for doubt or suspicion
- {不信感|ふしんかん}: distrust, mistrust — more neutral; can refer to specific distrust
- {警戒心|けいかいしん}: wariness, vigilance — more positive; implies reasonable caution
- {被害妄想|ひがいもうそう}: persecution complex — stronger; implies delusion

REGISTER:
Appears in literature, psychology, and formal writing. In everyday conversation, {疑|うたが}い{深|ぶか}い (suspicious, skeptical) is more natural.
